content.title: About
content.content: Blueberry syrup is a thick sweet syrup made from ripe blueberries, sugar and water. It has a bright berry aroma, a rich flavor with a hint of tartness and is used as an addition to drinks, desserts and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blueberries are rich in anthocyanins, which give them their characteristic blue color.
Traditionally, blueberry syrup was prepared in Northern Europe to preserve berries for winter.
The syrup can be used as a natural sweetener instead of sugar in cocktails.
In the United States, blueberry syrup is often served with pancakes and waffles.
Syrup stores longer than fresh berries when kept properly.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants in blueberries help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Vitamins C and K found in blueberries contribute to healthy vision.

items.title: Improves digestion
items.content: Fiber in the berries supports normal bowel function.

items.title: Reduces inflammation
items.content: Flavonoids may help lower inflammatory processes in the body.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The syrup contains a high amount of sugar, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Berry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to blueberries.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the syrup can irritate a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add blueberry syrup to tea, coffee, smoothies, yogurt, ice cream, pancakes, waffles and baked goods. It can also be used as a glaze for fruit or in marinades for meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the syrup in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator. When kept properly it retains its flavor for up to 6 months. Discard the product if it develops an off‑smell or color.
